candidates.summary: the carve-out's only end-to-end test asserts cur.IsCurrent(), which the VM makes true on every crossing entry, so it pins the abort and never the identity the exemption is there to preserve
candidates.failure_scenario: harnessSeedsCur widens or shifts (prefix match instead of equality, the frame index moving, the exemption firing for a deeper frame) and a foreign realm's cur is installed as the sub-test's frame identity instead of the entry aborting. TestCurSubtestAfterCross still passes: its only check is `if !cur.IsCurrent() { panic }` in curSubtestTarget, and the VM sets the entered cur as the current realm whatever realm it names, so that condition is false by construction. Flipping it to `if cur.IsCurrent()` fires the sentinel, proving the shipped panic is unreachable.
candidates.verify_by: cp reviews/pr/6xxx/6196-cur-binding-holes/1-6d88deba7/tests/b1-tests-r2-subtest-identity.gno over gnovm/tests/stdlibs/testing/cur_subtest_test.gno, then go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang/ -run 'TestStdlibs/test-testing': the sentinel panic fires, so the shipped assertion can never fail
candidates.evidence: with the sentinel in place: 'panic: SENTINEL: IsCurrent() was true' then '--- FAIL: TestCurSubtestAfterCross/sub (0.00s)'. Unmodified, the same command is '--- PASS: TestCurSubtestAfterCross (0.00s)'. What the test does pin is the abort: dropping '!m.harnessSeedsCur() && ' from op_call.go:513 turns it red with 'panic: crossing function testing_test func literal at cur_subtest_test.gno:18 was entered without cross()'.

candidates.summary: the write rule drops its realm-type test and legalises rebinding a realm-typed `cur` shadow for the first time, and the control that pins it ends before it reads the parameter back
candidates.failure_scenario: `cur := cur; cur = nil; p := &cur; *p = nil` inside a crossing function was refused at the merge base and is accepted at head; zrealm_cur_shadow.gno flipped from an expected rejection to a positive control in the same commit. Its main ends on println("ok") and never touches the parameter after the block, so a regression in which the shadow's slot aliased the crossing parameter, nulling the frame's identity, leaves the file green: nothing after the block reads cur. Adding `probe(cur)` after the block is the assertion that discriminates, and it passes at head.
